artists.biography: Anneke van Giersbergen (born March 8, 1973) was the singer in the Dutch band The Gathering from 1995 to 2007 when she announced her departure, summer 2007. She has since formed Agua de Annique with whom she released new songs in the fall of 2007. She has also worked with Devin Townsend Project, Danny Cavanagh & Anathema, Lawn, The Farmer Boys , Ayreon, Napalm Death, Globus, Moonspell, Giant Squid, Novembers Doom, Wetton/Downes, Maiden United and she has also done a live guest performance for Within Temptation. Her new album "The Darkest Skies Are The Brightest" is out now. Dianne van Giersbergen and Anneke van Giersbergen are both Dutch symphonic metal singers with the same last name. They are not related, but share a common last name, which is also the name of a small village in the Netherlands. They are both known for their strong vocal abilities and have achieved notable success in the symphonic metal scene. Read more on Last.fm. perplexity.description:
Anneke Van Giersbergen's album Drive was originally released in 2013 on Alone Records. Musically, the album blends melodic rock with elements of progressive and alternative rock, showcasing Van Giersbergen's signature powerful vocals and emotive songwriting. The arrangements are dynamic, featuring atmospheric textures, strong guitar work, and thoughtful production that highlights both her vocal range and the band's instrumental cohesion. Tracks like "We Live On" and the title song "Drive" exemplify her ability to merge introspective lyrics with accessible yet sophisticated rock melodies.

Drive stands as a pivotal release in Van Giersbergen's solo discography, following her departure from The Gathering and her earlier solo efforts. It further established her as a leading voice in progressive and alternative rock, demonstrating her growth as a songwriter and performer. The album received positive critical reception for its emotional depth and musical craftsmanship, with reviewers noting its balance between personal expression and broad appeal. While not a mainstream commercial blockbuster, Drive solidified Van Giersbergen's reputation among rock and prog fans for her consistent artistry and distinctive sound.
